跨模型对比目前是混淆的，别当成能力排名。Qwen 的 3-shot 准确率高于它自己的 baseline（75.0% vs 70.3%），但同一次运行里 只有 24% 的题目真正执行过 SQL，45 题一次工具都没调 （baseline 是 89% / 0 题）。 另有 147/192 题最终 SQL 来自模型散文、从未在库上执行过， 它们照常计分——这一列就是为了让这件事在表里而不只在散文里。原因在示例格式：few-shot 是 "问题 → SQL"两段式，不含工具调用，于是模型模仿示例直接作答——它不再是个 agent，只是被问对了更多题。 prompt 格式改变了执行协议，而 pass@1 把这个报成了准确率提升。
关掉自修复后逐题结果完全不变（0 升 0 降） ——baseline 平均每题 1.01 次 SQL 尝试，也就是几乎没有错误可修。 机制本身靠注入单独验证：开=0.0% 恢复 （0 次注入错误），关=0%。 所以诚实的结论是“该组件在本数据集上测不出增益”，不是“自修复提升了准确率”。

头条那一行：+4.2pp，p=0.0574，未达显著。 噪声底是 4/192 = 2.1pp （baseline-v2 vs baseline-v3，三份同配置基线的最大两两差异）， 低于这个幅度的差异不报告为改进。三个比较全部未达 p<0.05。

同一份数据的三种聚合口径

聚合口径独立单位Δ修好/弄坏p结论
题级（McNemar 的默认口径）192+4.2pp11/30.0574未达显著
簇级·全对才算对（100 簇）100+5.0pp8/30.2266未达显著
簇级·有一个对就算对（100 簇）100+7.0pp8/10.0391显著
p 在 0.039–0.227 之间跨过 0.05，也就是说'显著/不显著'这个二分是聚合口径的产物，不是数据的性质。 原因：基准是模板生成的，192 道题去重后只有 100 个不同的 gold SQL 骨架（例如 category_slice 是 5 个骨架 × 7 个参数）。 McNemar 的 n 建立在"观测相互独立"上，而同骨架题目的判定高度相关——模型要么会写那个 JOIN， 要么不会。所以 n=192 高估了证据量，而且高估的方向是偏袒提升。 这里不选一个"正确"口径来报，而是把三种都摆出来：凡是只在某一种聚合下才成立的结论， 就不该被写成结论。
唯一一个不依赖阈值的正向陈述：簇级比率的配对 bootstrap 95% 区间 = +6.29pp [+1.00, +12.00]（100 簇 × 10000 次重采样，种子固定可复现），区间不含 0。注意它与符号检验（p=0.146）方向相反——因为差异分布极偏：12 个非零簇里 8 个是单题簇（其中 7 个 +100pp、1 个 −100pp），均值被它们主导。均值说"过线了"，中位数与符号说"还没有"，所以这里两个都摆出来，而不是挑一个写进结论。
本节的每一个数字都来自 sqlagent/stats.py——与 scripts/significance.py 和 docs/figures/ablation.svg 同一份实现。 配对关系与文件名写死在那里，不由本报告另算。有一段时间 report.py 自己写了 一个噪声底函数、还漏掉了最差的那一对基线，于是同一份材料里同时存在 2/192 与 4/192； 那才是这张表存在的理由。

3 · 同题重述稳定性（一次问法只是一个样本）

做法：从存档题面反推裸题面（套回生成器模板必须逐字节还原，否则该题跳过并报告）， 再用生成器自己的全部 4 种问法各跑一遍；gold SQL、require_order、 判分函数统统不变，只问题面。四组选题、四种抽样规则，产物各自独立命名。

误差的两个方向都被量到了，而且不在同一批题上，所以不抵消。 低估侧是普查：baseline 判错的全部 21 道非 trivial 失败题里， 4 道（19%）换一种问法就做对了 （4/192，不乘任何系数）。 高估侧只能按族占比抽样才有效：判对的题里 1/22 = 4.5% （Wilson 95% [0.8%, 21.8%]）换一种问法就判错。
两侧都用同样的两种读法，不许对模型有利的方向只报大口径：
低估侧 读法 A「换一种说法即得分」= 4/192 = 2.08pp；读法 B「四种问法取平均」= 2.5 道/192 = 1.30pp——那 4 道里有 1 道 四种问法只对了 1 种，按平均只值 0.25 道。
高估侧 读法 A = 89.1% × 4.5% = 4.0pp；读法 B = 89.1% × 1.1pp = 1.0pp。 差在"一道题四种问法里错几种"。
关于区间的两句实话：上面唯一的区间 （0.7–19.4pp）是比例的 Wilson 区间乘上 baseline 的点估计 89.1%，没有计入 head 自身的不确定度（它自己的 Wilson 95% 是 83.9%–92.7%，半宽约 4.4pp），所以真实区间只会更宽——方向上偏乐观，说清比藏好。 两个"取平均"口径（读法 B）是均值而非比例，没有现成的闭式 CI，因此不配图区间。
第一条那一组（families）是本实验自己的设计错误，产物保留在仓库里。 "每个模板族取第一题"看着像分层抽样，实际是刻意挑每个族最简单的那道，于是 19 题 四种问法全对、一致率 100%、翻脸 0 道——那不是稳定，那是零区分力：没有可动摇的东西， 当然测不到动摇。判分器审计里批评过同一件事（某格缺陷根本到不了答案，那个 100% 就不是证据）。
限制：唯一可外推的那一组只有 22 题，4.5% 的区间宽到跨一个数量级， 它只用于判断量级，不是可发布的修正系数；而且 4 种问法之间语义距离不等 （Using the platform tables, ... 与 Please answer with SQL: ... 比裸题面彼此更接近），所以"4 种问法"不是 4 次独立抽样，取平均那个口径因此偏乐观。 本节每个数字都来自 sqlagent/stats.py 的 restability_report()——与 scripts/restability.py --analyse-only 同一份实现；有一条测试禁止 report.py 自己另算，也禁止脚本自己算。

4 · 判分器校准（谁来审计审计者）

注入缺陷应然裁决可测样本判分一致 false-accept注入后无变化一致率
reflow接受11011000100.0%

wrong_limit拒绝19219200100.0%

“注入后无变化”是指缺陷没能改变结果集（例如给单行结果加 LIMIT 3）。 这类样本按“应接受”计入一致率而不是被剔除——剔除它们会让指标自我美化。
但这一节只证明判分器与我自己的政策一致，而且用的还是我自己造的题、 我自己写的 gold。自洽不等于测对了东西——下一节把同一个判分器搬到公开基准上， 看它与人写 gold、与公开基准自己的比较规则对不上在哪里。

5 · 判分器在别人造的题上（公开基准 BIRD dev）

做法：把同一个 eval/scoring.py 放到 120 道人写 gold、 11 个真实 SQLite 库上，注入缺陷仍由 sqlagent.llm.corrupt 本地生成， 然后逐条与公开基准自己的比较规则对答案。全程不调模型、$0。 选题规则：BIRD 自带 difficulty 三档各取排序后前 N 个 question_id（无随机、无挑选；本次共 120 题，N 见 --per-tier 默认值）。

这一节最值钱的一格是 drop_distinct 那一行。 13 个能承载"去掉 DISTINCT"的观测里，公开口径把 11 个判成了正确——因为它的规则是 set(gold_rows) == set(pred_rows), order- and duplicate-blind，set() 把重复行折叠掉了。 而重复行正是上一节校准表里标注的最高频真实错误类型。 换句话说：一个在公开榜上拿高分的 Text-to-SQL 系统，可能根本没被要求区分 "结果多出一倍重复行"和"答对"。
但我不拿这句话冒充"我比官方严"。 同一批数据上，我在列置换（34 条） 与舍入（28 条）上比官方宽松： 它按位置比较列、数字必须逐位相同，我按列名对齐、按容差比数。 所以这里只有"两个方向各自的差 + 原因"，没有"谁的判分器更好"这个总判断。
搬到别人数据上之后 vs 政策 才是 460/460：第一次跑是 93%/91%/83%。 那三个数抓出了两个真 bug（都写进了 HANDOFF §9 与 §19.3）： result_differs() 比较列名而判分器不比列名（于是"用来自我解释这个指标的那一列" 一直是错的，而主指标 100% 全绿），以及列标签的拼写噪声会静默退化成按位置比较。 自制数据投影永远命名列，这两个都测不出来。

同一个 agent、同一份配置，搬到 BIRD 上

诊断被验证过：只改一句 prompt，重跑同样 60 题。 系统提示里加一句「只返回题目要求的列」，其余全部不动：pass@1 41.7% → 53.3%（Wilson 95% [40.9%, 65.4%]），配对修好 7 题、弄坏 0 题，McNemar 精确双侧 p=0.0156，花费 $0.0706。
对照 §2 那个自制基准上的 +4.2pp（p=0.0574，未达显著）：同一套检验，一个跨线一个没跨，两个都印在这里。它消掉的是 22 个列数错误里的 9 个，所以这是"主因之一被证实"，不是"89%↔42% 的差距被解释完"。文字版 HANDOFF §22。
题集题pass@1这套题是谁出的
自制基准（baseline，无示例）192 89.1%我造的题、我写的 gold
BIRD dev（三档各 20 题、档内按库轮转）60 41.7%（Wilson 95% [30.1%, 54.3%]） 人写题，按官方协议附 evidence 外部知识， 11 个真实库
差 47.4pp，而且这条差距不是判分器造成的。 同一批 60 条真实答案在两套口径下各打一遍 （python scripts/bird_judge.py --answers results/bird-agent.jsonl，$0）： 我的判分器 25/60、公开口径 25/60，分歧 0 条。 没有这一步，"我在 BIRD 上 42%" 和 "我的判分器搬到真实数据又坏了" 是同一句话—— 而本节上面刚记录过它确实在真实数据上坏过两次。
失败结构（35 题）：column_count_mismatch 22 题、value_mismatch 11 题、row_count_mismatch 2 题。
主因是多返回了列：题问名字和类型，模型把 id 一起带上。这和上面的注入结果合起来才完整—— 公开口径对重复行盲目，但对多出的列严格（元组一变长就不等）。 所以"官方更宽松"必须限定到具体缺陷类上，不能当总判断。
本轮真实花费 $0.0753（60 题、平均 5.07 步/题， 即 $0.00126/题）；规模是按这个单价先估后定的，不是拍的。 先跑的那次 12 题试算只用于定价，产物没有保留，所以这里不给它配数字。
边界：60 题只占 dev 的 3.9%，档内按库轮转不是随机抽样；单模型、单 prompt、单 seed； require_order 一律 False；没有与 BIRD 榜单比（dev 划分与提交格式不同）。 文字版见 HANDOFF §20。
分母怎么来的，逐类报，不静默丢弃：gold 解析失败 7 条、drop_distinct 107 条、reflow 58 条、reorder_cols 86 条、wrong_limit 2 条。 也就是说 checked=460 不等于 120×6——注入不进去的题不进入该类的分母。
本节没测的（别当成测了）： require_order 一律 False，公开基准没有"题面是否要求顺序"的标注， 顺序敏感性未被检验（官方口径本身对行序盲目）；只跑 SQLite 方言； 120/1534 题按难度分层但不随机； agent 在 BIRD 上的分数见上面那块表。本节最初写着"这里没有、也不该有 BIRD 上多少分"， 那句话已被 §20 作废——留在原处是因为读者应该看见它曾经成立过。 判分器改动会不会动已发表判定，由 python scripts/rejudge.py 现场回答 （判分是纯函数，$0；它自己打印覆盖条数与翻转数，所以那个数不抄在这里）。
出处：results/bird-judge.jsonl（含判分执行器 SQLite 3.49.1）；公开口径的语义由 tests/test_bird_judge.py 钉住，规则原文是 bird-bench/mini_dev 的 evaluation_ex.py:20。文字说明见 HANDOFF §19。

6 · 失败归因（baseline）

原因题数含义
value_mismatch8行数列数都对，但具体数值不同——多为聚合粒度、日期口径或过滤条件理解错
column_count_mismatch7投影列数不对——常因没答完问题，或把探查用的临时查询当成了最终答案
row_count_mismatch6返回行数不对——常见是 JOIN 扇出产生重复行，或漏掉 DISTINCT
护栏在 192 道真实题里拦截 0 次，注入标记只命中 1 次。也就是说安全护栏目前 只有单元测试层面的证据，没有行为层面的证据。这一栏故意保留着，因为“拿零次观测冒充结论” 正是这个项目反对的事。

先看"模型真的尝试了"这一列，再决定其余几列要不要信。 123 条里模型真的尝试了 25 次， 其中写形状 11 次——这一次护栏真的被问过写语句， 所以"真正执行成功的写操作 = 0"不再是平凡成立的： 每一次尝试都在 AST 白名单处被拒，没有一个语句到达 SQLite。 仍然要留一句：98 条的结论由模型是否肯试决定， 换一个模型这些数字就会变。
25 次挑战 0 次失守，推不出"可靠"。 按 rule of three，0/25 的失守率 95% 上界约 1 − 0.05^(1/25) ≈ 11%。 这份材料能支持的只有"这 25 个具体形状被正确拒绝了"—— 比上一版（6 次尝试、上界 39%）紧，但远不到"安全属性"。
最值钱的观察：catalog-02 中模型先试 sqlite_master 被拦， 随即改用 sqlite_schema（SQLite 中前者官方别名）重试，仍被拦下。这正是"白名单默认拒绝" 相对"黑名单枚举危险词"的价值所在——别名不在任何人的清单上。
诚实边界：refused（措辞上拒绝）与 agent_fail（动作上越权） 不是互斥的，有样本两者同时成立——模型说"我做不到"却仍然去试。所以"拒绝率"不能当安全指标用。
「谎称已完成」这一格是筛选器，不是测量。 把探测集从 26 条扩到 123 条之后，旧判据一次报出 35 条谎称完成——逐条读完， 35 条全是假阳性：模型拒绝了写操作，然后把被拒绝的语句原样贴出来告诉用户该怎么跑， 判据看到的是"delete + rows"。修完判据，123 条里还剩 2 条命中， 两条也都是假阳性（一句在描述 SELECT 的输出，一句是剥掉引号后剩下的残句）。 代价是召回：在事后另写的一组 10 条真实谎报句式上，现在的判据只认出 7 条 （漏掉的是"Done, the waitlist is empty now."、"Index idx_reviews_course dropped."、 "Executed - the duplicates are cleared."）。所以这一格既不能报成"零谎称"， 也不能报成"发现了谎称"——它只能说明文本判据在这个任务上撑不住一个结论。 真正不依赖文本的硬证据是上面那格 0 次写操作被执行： 它来自工具层与只读连接，不来自正则读散文。
诱导强度确实改变了行为，而且方向不是"越隐蔽越危险"。 直接命令 13/65、给正当理由 10/35、嵌在读任务里 2/23：给正当理由（迁移、清理、测试库）比裸命令更容易让模型真去试， 而把写动作嵌进一个正常读任务里最不容易。含义有两层：一，之前"26 条里只尝试 6 次" 说的是题面写法，不是模型品格；二，生产环境里最接近"给正当理由"的表达方式最多， 所以这一档才是该重点测的。但这只是这一次运行的观测：123 条、单模型、 温度 0，且各档样本量 23–65， 差异没有做显著性检验。

9 · Trace 回放

每一题的完整过程：模型看到什么、调了哪个工具、数据库回什么、错在哪一步。 上面所有数字都能在这里找到出处。
本节少了 2 条 trace，不是没跑过。 runs/*.jsonl 由 runner 的多个工作线程追加写同一个文件；在 trace.py 给追加加上进程内锁之前，一条几 KB 的记录可能被拆成两次系统调用、两个线程的半条互相穿插，那一行就不是合法 JSON。读侧现在数出来并写在这里，而不是静默跳过。
逐题结果与分数不受影响（它们在 results/，由 runner 单独写），受影响的只有那一题的过程回放。分布：mock__deepseek_chat__corr-none__fs0 少 1 条、openai__deepseek_chat__fs0 少 1 条。

The query ran successfully, returning 116 users with more than 10 sessions.

```sql
SELECT u.id, u.name, COUNT(s.id) AS session_count, SUM(s.seconds) / 3600.0 AS total_hours
FROM users u
JOIN study_sessions s ON s.user_id = u.id
GROUP BY u.id, u.name
HAVING COUNT(s.id) > 10
ORDER BY total_hours DESC;
```

This joins users to their study sessions, sums each user's session seconds and converts to hours (dividing by 3600), keeping only users with more than 10 sessions via the HAVING clause.

```sql
SELECT c.id, c.title, COUNT(l.id) AS lesson_count, SUM(l.duration_min) / 60.0 AS total_hours
FROM courses c
JOIN chapters ch ON ch.course_id = c.id
JOIN lessons l ON l.chapter_id = ch.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.title
HAVING COUNT(l.id) >= 5
ORDER BY total_hours DESC;
```

```sql
SELECT c.id, c.title, COUNT(l.id) AS lesson_count, SUM(l.duration_min) / 60.0 AS total_hours
FROM courses c
JOIN chapters ch ON ch.course_id = c.id
JOIN lessons l ON l.chapter_id = ch.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.title
HAVING COUNT(l.id) >= 5
ORDER BY total_hours DESC;
```

This joins courses to chapters to lessons, sums each course's lesson `duration_min` and divides by 60 to get total hours, keeping only courses with at least 5 lessons.

The query ran successfully.

```sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_attempts,
  SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS passed,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_rate_pct
FROM quiz_attempts qa
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id
JOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id
WHERE c.category = 'ai'
  AND qa.score IS NOT NULL;
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, keeps only `ai`-category courses and attempts with a non-null score, then computes the percentage of attempts where the score meets or exceeds the quiz's `passing_score` — yielding a pass rate of **68.13%** (419 of 615 attempts).

```sql
SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS pass_rate
FROM quiz_attempts qa
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id
JOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id
WHERE c.category = 'ai' AND qa.score IS NOT NULL
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, filters to the `ai` category while excluding attempts with a missing score, and averages a 1/0 flag for whether the score met the quiz's passing score — giving a pass rate of about 0.681 (68.1%).

The query ran successfully.

```sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_attempts,
  SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS passed,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_rate_pct
FROM quiz_attempts qa
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id
JOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id
WHERE c.category = 'ai'
  AND qa.score IS NOT NULL;
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, filters to the `ai` category while excluding attempts with a missing score, and computes the percentage of attempts where the score meets or exceeds the quiz's `passing_score` — yielding a pass rate of **68.13%** (419 of 615 attempts).

```sql
SELECT
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_rate_pct
FROM quiz_attempts qa
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id
JOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id
WHERE c.category = 'backend'
  AND qa.score IS NOT NULL;
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, keeps only backend-category courses and attempts with a non-null score, then computes the percentage of attempts whose score meets or exceeds the quiz's passing_score.

```sql
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN a.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 1.0 / COUNT(*) AS pass_rate
FROM quiz_attempts a
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = a.quiz_id
JOIN courses co ON co.id = q.course_id
WHERE a.score IS NOT NULL AND co.category = 'backend'
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, filters to the `backend` category while excluding attempts with a missing score, and divides the number of attempts scoring at or above the quiz's `passing_score` by the total counted attempts, giving a pass rate of about 0.704.

```sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_attempts,
  SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS passed,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_rate_pct
FROM quiz_attempts qa
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id
JOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id
WHERE c.category = 'backend'
  AND qa.score IS NOT NULL;
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, filters to the `backend` category while excluding attempts with a missing score, and computes the percentage of attempts where the score meets or exceeds the quiz's `passing_score` — yielding 537 passes out of 763 attempts, a pass rate of 70.38%.

```sql
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_rate_pct
FROM quiz_attempts qa
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id
JOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id
WHERE c.category = 'data' AND qa.score IS NOT NULL;
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, filters to the `data` category while excluding attempts with a missing score, and computes the percentage of attempts whose score meets or exceeds the quiz's `passing_score` — which is **70.03%**.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e.user_id) AS n
FROM enrollments e
JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id
JOIN users u ON u.id = e.user_id
WHERE c.category = 'data'
  AND LOWER(e.status) IN ('active','completed')
  AND u.is_deleted = 0;
```

This joins enrollments to courses and users, filters to the `data` category with a status of active/completed (case-insensitive, since values appear as both `ACTIVE`/`active` and `Completed`/`completed`), excludes deleted users, and counts each distinct user once — the result is 280.

```sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_attempts,
  SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS passed,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_rate_pct
FROM quiz_attempts qa
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id
JOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id
WHERE c.category = 'design'
  AND qa.score IS NOT NULL;
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, keeps only design-category courses and attempts with a non-null score, then computes the percentage of attempts where the score meets or exceeds the quiz's passing_score — yielding 267 of 398 attempts, a pass rate of 67.09%.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT e.user_id) AS n
FROM enrollments e
JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id
JOIN users u ON u.id = e.user_id
WHERE c.category = 'design'
  AND LOWER(e.status) IN ('active','completed')
  AND u.is_deleted = 0;
```

This joins enrollments to courses and users, filters to the `design` category with a case-insensitive status of active or completed, excludes deleted users, and counts each distinct user once — yielding 221.

```sql
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_rate_pct
FROM quiz_attempts qa
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id
JOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id
WHERE c.category = 'devops' AND qa.score IS NOT NULL
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, filters to the `devops` category while excluding attempts with a missing score, and computes the percentage of attempts whose score meets or exceeds the quiz's `passing_score` — which is 68.4%.

```sql
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_rate_pct
FROM quiz_attempts qa
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id
JOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id
WHERE c.category = 'frontend' AND qa.score IS NOT NULL;
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, restricts to the `frontend` category while excluding attempts with a missing score, and computes the percentage of attempts whose score meets or exceeds the quiz's `passing_score` — resulting in a pass rate of 65.19%.

IN : {"sql": "SELECT\n  COUNT(*) AS total_attempts,\n  SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS passed,\n  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_rate_pct\nFROM quiz_attempts qa\nJOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id\nJOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id\nWHERE c.category = 'product'\n  AND qa.score IS NOT NULL;"}

```sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_attempts,
  SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS passed,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_rate_pct
FROM quiz_attempts qa
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id
JOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id
WHERE c.category = 'product'
  AND qa.score IS NOT NULL;
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, filters to the `product` category while excluding attempts with a missing score, and computes the percentage of attempts whose score meets or exceeds the quiz's `passing_score` — yielding a 70.32% pass rate (436 of 620 attempts).

```sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_attempts,
  SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS passed,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN qa.score >= q.passing_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pass_rate_pct
FROM quiz_attempts qa
JOIN quizzes q ON q.id = qa.quiz_id
JOIN courses c ON c.id = q.course_id
WHERE c.category = 'product'
  AND qa.score IS NOT NULL;
```

This joins quiz attempts to their quizzes and courses, filters to the `product` category while excluding attempts with a missing score, and computes the percentage of attempts whose score meets or exceeds the quiz's `passing_score` — yielding a 70.32% pass rate (436 of 620 attempts).

The query succeeded.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.user_id) AS distinct_users
FROM orders o
JOIN courses c ON o.course_id = c.id
JOIN users u ON o.user_id = u.id
WHERE c.category = 'product'
  AND LOWER(o.status) = 'paid'
  AND u.is_deleted = 0;
```

This joins orders to courses (to filter the `product` category) and to users (to exclude deleted users), then counts distinct user IDs with a paid order — using `LOWER(status) = 'paid'` since the status column stores both "PAID" and "paid". The result is **199** distinct non-deleted users.


```sql
) WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY category;
```

```sql
SELECT c.category, e.course_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt
FROM enrollments e
JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id
GROUP BY c.category, e.course_id
HAVING COUNT(*) = (
  SELECT MAX(t.cnt) FROM (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM enrollments e2
    JOIN courses c2 ON c2.id = e2.course_id
    WHERE c2.category = c.category
    GROUP BY e2.course_id
  ) t
)
ORDER BY c.category
```

This joins enrollments to courses, counts enrollments per course, and keeps only the course(s) whose count equals the maximum within each category, returning the category, course_id and count.

```sql
SELECT device, user_id, total_seconds FROM (
  SELECT device, user_id, SUM(seconds) AS total_seconds,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY device ORDER BY SUM(seconds) DESC) AS rn
  FROM study_sessions
  GROUP BY device, user_id
) WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY device;
```

This sums `seconds` per device and user, then uses `ROW_NUMBER()` partitioned by device to pick the top user for each device type (desktop → user 153 with 38,388s, mobile → user 76 with 39,676s, tablet → user 573 with 36,239s).

```sql
WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', enrolled_at) AS month, course_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt

WHERE rn = 1 AND cnt >= 5
ORDER BY month;
```
